assertions.name: parseval_exact_over_full_class_basis
assertions.note: SUM_{mu != 1^k} b_mu^2 = Var_P(ln f) to 1e-9 at every k -- the expansion is complete, which is the check that the coefficients are right

assertions.name: ln_f_is_supported_on_even_classes
assertions.note: ln f is omega-even, so its odd-class mass is 0; measured ~1e-30 relative, i.e. numerically exact

assertions.name: mass_is_at_degree_two_not_degree_one
assertions.note: d=2 carries 50.0% against d=1's 19.4% at k=16. SELF-CORRECTION: #7051 argued ln f has no terminating Kerov expansion from the d=1 share alone, which does not follow -- the Sigma_p generate the algebra MULTIPLICATIVELY, and the mass is at d=2

assertions.name: no_fixed_degree_suffices
assertions.note: d<=2 cumulative falls 90.5% (k=8) -> 69.4% (k=16). The #7051 conclusion survives, now on evidence that supports it

assertions.name: sigma3_is_a_single_basis_vector
assertions.note: |C_{(3,1^{k-3})}| = (k)_3/3, so Sigma_3 = (k)_3/sqrt(|C_3|) * e_3 is ONE orthonormal basis vector. Hence Cov_P(ln f, Sigma_3) is one Fourier coefficient of ln f, and every d>=2 mode -- the 50-66% of the mass measured above -- is orthogonal to it and contributes nothing. Whether the expansion terminates has no bearing on the conjecture

assertions.name: G_of_zero_vanishes_as_exact_integers
assertions.note: W+ = W- as EXACT integers for 4 <= k <= 22. This is G(0) = 0, i.e. column orthogonality, and it is what makes the sign-split a pair of probability measures with equal total mass

assertions.name: G_is_negative_on_the_open_interval
assertions.note: E_{nu+}[f^s] < E_{nu-}[f^s] at s = .25,.5,.75,1 for every k tested: partitions whose 3-cycle character is NEGATIVE carry the larger dimensions. s=1 is the conjecture itself

assertions.name: first_order_dominance_is_FALSE
assertions.note: nu- does NOT stochastically dominate nu+ in f^lam. Exact on Fractions: fails at k=18 (gap 0.0161) and k=26 (gap 0.0011), holds at the other 21 values in 10..32. It would have given G(s) <= 0 for ALL s >= 0. ELIMINATED

assertions.name: increasing_concave_dominance_is_FALSE
assertions.note: Second-order (increasing-concave) dominance is strictly WEAKER and exactly matched to the exponents that matter -- x^s is increasing concave for s in (0,1) -- so the FSD failure did not settle it. It fails at the SAME two k. ELIMINATED

assertions.name: conjecture_still_holds_at_the_failing_k
assertions.note: Decided on exact Fractions: E_{nu+}[f] <= E_{nu-}[f] -- i.e. G(1) = T_3(k) <= 0 -- holds at BOTH k=18 and k=26. So those k break the dominance STRUCTURE, not the conjecture, which is what makes the two orders strictly stronger than needed and strictly false

parameters.claim: the Kerov-expansion question is orthogonal to the conjecture (one coefficient); FSD and ICV on the sign-split both fail at k=18 and k=26
